- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses early trend reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead of true reversal.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3–5-day moving average.
- When sentiment is low but price is rising, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.0% per day).
